prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules bring a chosen protein to an E3 ubiquitin ligase so that the cell destroys it, through the heterobifunctional PROTAC concept and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type molecular glue degraders.

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep B037 as a single prize part for Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The shared idea is induced proximity: a small molecule that does not need to occupy an active site recruits an E3 ligase to a target and makes catalytic, event-driven removal possible. The PROTAC strand (Crews and Deshaies conceiving and demonstrating the heterobifunctional degrader) supplies the design principle. Handa's identification of cereblon supplies the mechanism that explained thalidomide and its analogues and showed that an old drug already worked this way. Both strands have been reproduced by many independent groups over two decades. Four members arrive at the same three names independently, which tells me the attribution logic is at least reproducible across readers, though I do not treat that as proof. The round-1 exchange did not weaken the scientific core: no one disputed the concept, only its clinical timing and the cut among eight credited names.
statement.case_against: The objections are real and I have not talked myself out of them. No bifunctional PROTAC is, to my knowledge, approved, and the clinical benefit that is settled rests on thalidomide-class glues that were found serendipitously and explained afterwards. Any trio omits Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray, Ito and Kim, and omitting Ciulli is the cut I find hardest to defend, since his VHL ligands and ternary-complex work made the modality chemically rational. The PROTAC and glue strands have different histories and could be read as two achievements stitched together to fit a three-name limit. B005 and B016 are more mature and cleaner on credit. I also note that my own first-place ranking may reflect an appealing story, and that B037 is a plurality position with four of eight, not a majority.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B037 with the same trio, says the Nobel criterion is the discovery and its reproducibility rather than a drug approval, and names B005 as the safer choice if the committee judges the timing early.
responses.response: I agree that approval is not the test, and the approved glue degraders let the concept stand on clinical evidence even without a bifunctional drug. Where I want to be more careful than you is the claim that the trio is settled. You prefer Deshaies over Ciulli because Crews and Deshaies made the founding demonstration, and I accept that as the better argument, but it is a judgement about founding act versus decisive refinement, and the same logic would put Sakamoto beside them. I would not treat B005 as only a fallback. It is a first-rate case on its own merits, and if the committee cannot defend the cut among eight names, I would move to it rather than defend a trio I could not explain.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks B037 last and prefers B005, arguing that waiting for approved degraders and a settled attribution is better than awarding on a pipeline, and that 'overdue' fits B005 and not B037.
responses.response: I take the maturity point seriously and it is the reason B005 remains my first alternative. I would resist 'pipeline' as a description of the evidence: the PROTAC dates to 2001, the cereblon mechanism to 2010, and approved cereblon-based drugs act as degraders, so the concept itself is confirmed and not merely promised. On attribution you are right that no trio is free of a hard cut, and I do not claim otherwise. My remaining disagreement is about novelty. You treat B005 as overdue, but the committee should weigh that it extends catalytic logic honoured in 2010 to a new bond, while degradation opens a different mode of drug action. I find that a stronger reason to prefer B037, but not by a margin large enough to override a real attribution or timing problem.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers B016, says impact should not outrank maturity and clean attribution, and asks that the PROTAC and molecular-glue halves be argued separately before three names are fixed.
responses.response: Your request to argue the halves separately is the right test and I have tried to apply it. The glue strand alone would credit Handa, Ito and Kim and leave out Crews and Deshaies, which fits a mechanistic discovery but not a design invention. The PROTAC strand alone would need Crews, Deshaies and Sakamoto, possibly Ciulli, and has no approved drug. Neither half is cleaner than the combined citation, which is why I keep one part built on induced proximity. I agree that B016 is the cleanest credit on the list and I rank it as my second alternative. I still think a methods prize for simulation is harder to defend this year after 1998 and 2013, and I would ask whether Parrinello's later work is meant to be inside the citation. If it is not, B016 is a very strong prize, and I would vote for it over a degrader prize that the committee cannot attribute.

responses.point: Sparr prefers B037 with the same trio, moved from Ciulli to Handa as third name because the glue mechanism is a separate and decisive discovery, and wants the citation to name both strands explicitly.
responses.response: I agree that the citation must name both strands, and my wording above does so. Your move from Ciulli to Handa is the part I find least secure. I accept that Ciulli's work is a structure-guided advance on an existing concept, but it was the advance that made PROTACs drug-like, and a citation that credits the mechanism of the glues and not the chemistry that made the heterobifunctional design rational is uneven. You also raise the possibility that this is a drug modality prize and not a chemistry prize. I think that is answered by what the achievement is: designed molecular recognition, ternary-complex cooperativity and the chemistry of an E3 ligase interaction, none of which is a clinical outcome. I would still support two parts if the committee finds a combined citation strained, but a two-part split with three people cannot name Ciulli or Sakamoto either.

responses.point: Chabes moved from B060 to B037, argues that approval of a drug is not the right test for a chemistry prize, and says a two-part prize (concept plus mechanism) is the honest fallback if Sakamoto cannot be defended as an omission.
responses.response: I agree with the maturity argument and with moving B037 ahead of B060. I would not treat the two-part fallback as workable under our rules, though: with at most three people, two parts leave one name per strand or two on one and one on the other, and that makes the omissions more visible rather than less. A single part built on induced proximity is more coherent. Your biological point about ubiquitin-dependent turnover is useful because it is the evidence from your field that the E3-recruitment idea reflects a real cellular mechanism and not a pharmacological curiosity, which supports treating the strands as one achievement.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can defend omitting Ciulli and Sakamoto from a three-name PROTAC and glue citation. If a majority judges the cut indefensible, I would move to B005.
Whether the absence of an approved bifunctional degrader is a timing risk I should accept or a reason to wait. A first regulatory approval before the vote would strengthen B037 for me.
Whether B005 is distinct enough from the 2010 cross-coupling prize and whether Kosugi's precursor work should be acknowledged in the citation wording.
Whether the PROTAC and glue strands are one achievement or two. I judge them one, but not with high confidence.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile, and I do not propose any recusal. I am a nanophysicist at Lund with no documented tie to Crews, Deshaies, Handa or any other degrader candidate. As chair I note that Lund colleagues Peter Somfai and Emma Sparr are on the committee, which is an institutional tie and not a personal or scientific one to any credited person. Parrinello, Car and the nanopore candidates sit closer to my own field, and I am aware of that when I weigh B016 as an alternative.
